column1: # The `--json` contract of the one command surface (T4): which schema document each verb
# answers with. Tab-separated, one row per verb:
#   verb      the verb, as the dash-joined path a walk of the clap tree reaches it by
#   document  the type it emits, as `schemas/webcam-handler-schema.json` keys it under `$defs`
# **Three readers, which is why this is a file and not a table inside one of them.**
# proves it names exactly the verbs the clap tree offers — in both directions, so a verb added
# without a row and a row naming a verb that was renamed are each a red test at workspace
# scope. `webcam-handler-xtask` prints it into the agent usage guide, which is how the guide
# tells an agent which document to expect without anybody retyping the mapping.
# `scripts/gates/json-validates.sh` runs each verb over the fake backend and validates the
# answer against the `$defs` entry named here.
# Until docs/7 P6e this mapping lived in the gate alone, as the one thing that predicate
# writes down rather than derives; the guide would have been its second hand-written copy,
# which is exactly the drift P6e exists to prevent (note **N122**).
# A `$defs` name that no longer exists in the bundle fails `json-validates.sh`; a verb with
# no row here fails `cli_core`'s test *and* the gate's `--help` walk.
